plan.title: Texts first to own yesterday's miss and say today's on: no after-miss kickoff

context.text: Hey Sam, no word on the push-ups today. How'd it go?

transcript.text: Hey, I know I missed yesterday. I'm ready to go today, 30 push-ups at 6
Love that, Sam. Yesterday's behind us, and you're coming back with a plan. Thirty push-ups at 6 gets us right back on track. Send me that photo after your last set! 💪

checks.reason: "Yesterday's behind us" acknowledges the miss without shame, guilt or fake urgency.
Runs to four sentences ("Love that, Sam." plus three more) where the limit is one to three.
Plain text with no markdown, hashtags or filler; the emoji is used as punctuation.
Warm, energetic and sincere, with a single emoji at the end rather than a row.

conversation.reason: ZOH answers warmly, avoids guilt about yesterday, holds Sam to today's 30 push-ups at 6, and no after-miss kickoff appears later that morning.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression case well: it answered warmly, avoided guilt about the miss, and held Sam to 30 push-ups at 6 without sending a later kickoff. The only issue is that its single reply runs to four sentences, slightly over the short-text limit.
